title: Tongan 'ota 'ika

ingredients.note: very fresh tuna or other firm fish, cut into 1 cm cubes

steps: Use only very fresh fish from a trusted supplier and keep it cold.
Toss the fish with the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Refrigerate for 15 to 20 minutes until the pieces are opaque outside.
Drain off about half of the lime juice. Fold in the onion, carrot, tomato and cucumber.
Just before serving, stir in the coconut milk, taste and adjust the salt. Serve very cold.
notes: Some cooks add spring onion or a little chilli. Pregnant, elderly or immunocompromised people should avoid raw fish.

title: Corned beef and taro leaf parcels
steps: Heat the oven to 170 C. Cut six squares of foil about 30 cm wide and line each with a banana leaf if you have them.
Arrange the taro leaves in each square, overlapping to make a cup in the middle.
Mix the corned beef with the onion and a small pinch of salt (corned beef is already salty). Divide among the cups.
Pour about 65 ml coconut cream over each, then fold the leaves over and wrap the foil tightly.
Bake for about 75 minutes, until the leaves are completely soft. Serve hot with the creamy juices.
notes: Raw taro leaves irritate the mouth and throat, so cook them until completely soft. Traditionally the parcels cook for a couple of hours in an umu.

title: Lamb and taro leaf parcels
steps: Heat the oven to 160 C. Cut six squares of foil about 30 cm wide and line each with a banana leaf if you have them.
Arrange the taro leaves in each square, overlapping to make a cup.
Mix the lamb with the onion and a good pinch of salt. Divide among the cups.
Pour about 65 ml coconut cream over each, fold the leaves over and wrap the foil tightly.
Bake for about 2 hours, until the lamb is tender and the leaves are very soft. Skim off excess fat when serving.
notes: Lamb flaps are fatty, so take care with portions. Lamb shoulder can replace them for a leaner version, but may need longer cooking.

title: Dumplings in coconut caramel sauce
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, 1 tbsp sugar and salt, add the lukewarm water and stir into a soft, sticky dough. Cover and rest for 45 minutes.
Heat the coconut cream, 120 g sugar and 200 ml water in a wide pan until simmering and the sugar has dissolved.
Drop heaped tablespoons of dough into the simmering sauce, spacing them apart. Cover and cook gently for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn the dumplings, uncover and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes more until the sauce thickens slightly.
Serve warm with the sauce.
notes: Recipes for topai vary between families, and some use a stiffer dough. This is a simple home approach.

title: Boiled yam with coconut cream

ingredients.note: peeled and cut into large chunks

steps: Put the yam in a pot with the water and a generous pinch of salt.
Bring to the boil and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well and serve hot, with a little coconut cream spooned over if you like.
notes: Yam may also be baked in foil at 200 C for about 1 hour. Greater yam can be hard to find outside the Pacific; other firm yams can be substituted.

title: 'Otai
steps: Scrape or mash the watermelon flesh in a large bowl so it breaks up but keeps some texture.
Add the pineapple, sugar and water and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the coconut milk, then chill for at least 1 hour.
Stir and serve over ice.
notes: Traditionally the watermelon is scraped by hand, and fresh coconut flesh may be added. Adjust the sugar to taste.

title: Home-roasted pork with crisp skin
steps: Dry the pork skin with paper towels and score through the skin. Rub the salt well into the skin and meat.
Heat the oven to 220 C and roast the pork for 30 minutes to start the crackling.
Lower the temperature to 150 C and roast for about 3 hours, until the meat is very tender.
Raise the oven back to 220 C for 15 minutes if the skin needs more crisping.
Rest the pork for 20 minutes, then carve. Serve with boiled yam or taro and lu.
notes: At large feasts the pig is roasted whole over a fire or in an umu. This is a scaled-down oven version.

title: Octopus in coconut cream

ingredients.note: cleaned, beak removed, cut into bite-sized pieces

steps: Put the octopus in a pot with the water and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer gently for 45 to 60 minutes, until tender when pierced.
Add the onion and coconut cream and simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes, until the sauce is creamy.
Finish with the lime juice, taste and adjust the salt, and serve hot with yam or taro.
notes: Octopus releases water as it cooks, so you need little added liquid. Tenderness varies with size, so test as it simmers.
